items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: And then meeting Mr. Johnson, too, and then I didn't mess around with the bad element of the fellas.

ctx.x: girlfriend. What's that? Okay, so you're discharged. Yeah. And so now that you're out, what was the prospects of your life at that point? Well, my prospect was, yeah. Maybe I could back up a little bit. How did you view the Navy

and how did it change your life? Well, okay, yeah. The Navy, to me, the Navy was a big asset in me being who I am today. Because, like I said, I went in the day I made seventeen. I was a little kid with a child of mine and all this. And going into the service, then, I had three years on my own, you know, being my own man, under command of somebody. And that's why I think today that the service is good for some people because if you, first of all, if you can take orders, live with them, take orders and live with…
Something we haven't really talked about, and we can get back to that, to what you did. What did your parents tell you about whites, about whites, and how to behave?
